fragments.exact_quote: In PTX, the fundamental types reflect the native data types supported by the target architectures. A fundamental type specifies both a basic type and a size. Register variables are always of a fundamental type, and instructions operate on these types. The same type-size specifiers are used for both variable definitions and for typing instructions, so their names are intentionally short.

fragments.exact_quote:
Bits (untyped): .b8, .b16, .b32, .b64, .b128
Most instructions have one or more type specifiers, needed to fully specify instruction behavior. Operand types and sizes are checked against instruction types for compatibility.
Two fundamental types are compatible if they have the same basic type and are the same size. Signed and unsigned integer types are compatible if they have the same size. The bit-size type is compatible with any fundamental type having the same size.

known_evidence_gaps.description: Whether source operand `a` may be an immediate constant in or.b32 is not explicitly shown in 9.7.8.2; the documented or.b32 example uses an immediate in `b` position only (or.b32 mask, mask,0x00010001).
Whether destination `_` is permitted for scalar or.b32 is not explicit in 9.7.8.2; only the general PTX 9.2 rule (bit bucket may replace destination) is available.
No explicit error, trap, or undefined-behavior clause for or (or.b32) was found in the sections read. This absence is not treated as a semantic claim.

The combination of operand-size/compatibility rules (same-size rule, bit-size compatibility, and the Notes sentence "allowed types include predicates") requires semantic-phase interpretation to resolve all admissible source types for or.b32.
